comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the no-pooled-capital part is what makes it workable. the hard bit comes when the macro person and the chart person disagree on the same ticker on the same day, somebody has to decide whose read wins or it turns into a group chat.

replies.author: castironsteel7
replies.body: I may have been a little misleading when I mentioned the option of taking on risk. I’m really hoping for an alpha seeking collective. Maybe the macro guy knows of some niche binary phenomenon and he gets with the person who mainly trades derivatives. Ultimately they could both discover an applicable trading system considering it’s not a one time event. Everybody can still trade autonomously if they choose.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: then the shared piece is the testing, not the money. write the macro trigger and the derivatives leg as one rule, run it over every past occurrence, and the argument becomes about the numbers. that's roughly why I made Quantradin, everyone sees the same paper results for one written rule. free, quantradin.com
